text:
mason: Nightly 'mesh-e2e' on the l40 pool is red — native-kernel-smoke step failing with a PTX/JIT error. tail of the container log below. 

mason: ```
[2025-11-03T06:12:34Z] cudaJitLinkCreate: PTX → cubin failed: no kernel image is available for execution on the device
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): CUDA kernel launch failed: invalid device function
/opt/runner/work/mesh/mesh/tests/native_kernels.cc:142: in run_kernel()
```

mason: CI job: job/45821, image: ghcr.io/redwood/ci-base:cuda12.2-l40-20251102. Not seeing OOM, it fails immediately during module load. :eyes:

ci-bot: Rerun command: `/ci rerun job/45821` (last run by @mason)

kai: can you paste the full docker image tag and the kernel compute capability? l40 can be heterogeneous (a100/l40 mix) so PTX might not match.

mason: image tag above. The node labels show l40-2 and l40-7 in the matrix for that shard. I suspect one host is on driver 535.* and another on 545.* which could cause missing cubin for a JITed PTX.

amanda: quick check: can someone try a targeted rerun on the single-host pool: `pool=l40-stable-545`? if it passes there it's driver skew.

devops-bot: Recording artifact locations: gs://redwood-ci/mesh/job-45821/logs.tar.gz and attached node metadata: node=l40-7 driver=545.23, node=l40-2 driver=535.12.

mason: thanks — doing a `/ci rerun --pool l40-stable-545 job/45821` now.

ci-bot: Rerun queued as job/45826 against pool l40-stable-545.

kai: if the rerun passes, we should pin the nightly matrix to the intersection of supported drivers or add a fallback to precompiled cubins. Also useful to try reproducing locally with the same image:

kai: ```bash
docker run --gpus all --rm -e NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility 
  -v $(pwd):/workspace ghcr.io/redwood/ci-base:cuda12.2-l40-20251102 
  bash -lc "python -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0))' && python tests/native_kernels_repro.py"
```

amanda: other quick mitigation: set `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY` in the runtime to delay JIT and avoid immediate module link failures during warmup. Worth trying if rerun still flakes.

mason: rerun job/45826 started. I'll dump the kernel link logs once it finishes. If it passes on 545-only pool, I'll open a small follow-up to restrict mixes until we build multi-arch cubins.

amanda: if it fails again, please trigger a bisect across the base image layers. @kai can you help with a bisect plan? we may need to check when the system default NVPTX arch flags changed.

kai: yep — plan: 1) reproduce locally with same image, 2) try driver 535 vs 545 locally (we have a spare node), 3) if repro is deterministic, do incremental base-image rollbacks to find the layer that changed ptx arch flags. I'll slot time later today. :+1:

mason: job/45826 passed on l40-stable-545. seems driver skew was the immediate cause. I'm going to document the incidence and open a follow-up asking to standardize l40 nightly pools to the newer driver, plus a short-term fallback to prebuilt cubins.

amanda: sweet. thanks for the quick triage. please add notes to the job and tag infra-owner. :thumbsup:

mason: adding notes and creating issue INFRA-1298. tagging infra on the issue.

devops-bot: Issue INFRA-1298 created by mason: "l40 nightly: driver skew -> PTX JIT failures; standardize driver or include precompiled cubins"

mason: closing thread for now; re-open if we see regressions.
